  • cut_breaks() — Cut at chosen cutpoints, extending end intervals to the observed range
  • cut_length() — Cut numeric values into equal-width intervals; labels = FALSE returns integer codes
  • cut_quantile() — Alias of xtile() Stata: xtile

  • destring() — Convert to numbers, dropping value labels

  • duplicates_list() — List duplicated rows
  • duplicates_report() — Count duplicated rows
  • duplicates_tag() — Mark duplicated rows
  • encode() — Encode character categories as labelled integer codes; preserve factor codes Stata: encode
  • findit() — Find the R equivalent of a Stata command
  • findit_clip() — Look up one Stata command from the clipboard
  • findit_selection() — Look up one selected Stata command in the source editor
  • fre() — Joint frequency table like tab(), adding totals and displaying value labels
  • fre1() — One one-way table per variable like tab1(), adding totals and displaying value labels Stata: tab1
  • fre2() — Pairwise cross-tabulations like tab2(), adding totals and row labels; column headers keep category codes Stata: tabulate
  • is_first() — Mark the first row of each group
  • isid() — Confirm unique keys with a message and return data invisibly; .missing allows missing keys and empty strings
  • misstable() — Missing values per variable, or missing-value patterns
  • mvdecode() — Turn given codes into missing values
  • mvencode() — Replace missing values with a code
  • na_if_value() — Alias of mvdecode() Stata: mvdecode
  • pc() — Percentage of the total, not a percentile rank; prop = TRUE returns proportions
  • pct() — Removed alias of pc(); use pc() for total shares and dplyr::percent_rank() for percentile ranks Stata: egen pc()
  • preview() — Persist a head/tail or interval console preview (10 data rows by default), retaining every row and column
  • preview_headtail() — Persist a first-and-last-row preview; a row of dots marks an omitted middle; all data are retained
  • preview_interval() — Persist an approximately evenly spaced row preview without separator rows, retaining all data
  • print_headtail() — Print first and last rows once with a dotted omission row; return the complete input invisibly without changing preview preferences
  • print_interval() — Print approximately evenly spaced rows once without separator rows; return the complete input invisibly without changing preview preferences
  • pwcorr() — Pearson or Spearman correlations with pairwise samples by default; .listwise keeps p-values on one common sample; optional Bonferroni or Sidak adjustment within each group
  • recode() — Alias of stata_recode() Stata: recode
  • row_max() — Maximum across variables in each row
  • row_mean() — Mean across variables in each row
  • row_median() — Median across variables in each row
  • row_min() — Minimum across variables in each row
  • row_miss() — Number of missing values in each row
  • row_non_miss() — Number of observed values in each row
  • row_nvals() — Number of distinct values in each row, ignoring missing values
  • row_sd() — Standard deviation across variables in each row
  • row_sum() — Sum across variables in each row
  • row_unique() — Number of distinct values in each row, counting missing as one Stata: egen rownvals()
  • row_var() — Sample variance across variables in each row
  • select_or_transmute() — Return selected and computed columns, retaining grouping columns
  • set_seed() — Set the random seed, alone or at the end of a pipe
  • spearman() — Unweighted Spearman rank correlations on one common complete-case sample by default; .pairwise uses separate samples; returns r, n and Stata 18+ p-values with optional within-group adjustment
  • stata_diff() — Difference from the previous period, respecting time gaps
  • stata_lag() — Value from an earlier period, respecting time gaps
  • stata_lead() — Value from a later period, respecting time gaps
  • stata_merge() — Merge two tables and report matches, like Stata's merge
  • stata_recode() — Recode numeric values with Stata-style ranges, value sets and labels; unmatched values are kept
  • std() — Z-scores: subtract the observed mean and divide by the sample SD
  • summ() — Summary statistics for variables
  • tab() — Count joint category combinations in one long table with frequencies and percentages
  • tab1() — One one-way frequency table per variable; returns a list by default
  • tab2() — Wide cross-tabulations for every variable pair; explicit .by creates grouped tables
  • tab_gen() — Alias of as_dummy() Stata: tabulate, generate()
  • tabstat() — Chosen statistics for variables, optionally by group
  • timer() — Time how long code takes
  • tostring() — Convert to text, keeping codes rather than value labels
  • unpreview() — Restore ordinary printing by removing preview preferences, retaining all data and grouping
  • value_if_na() — Alias of mvencode() Stata: mvencode
  • var_type() — Describe storage type or class, optionally using an abbreviation
  • var_unit() — Read measurement or duration units; return NA_character_ when absent
  • variables() — List variables with their types and labels
  • variables_search() — Find variables by name or label
  • varlist() — Select variables with Stata wildcards such as x*
  • xtile() — Quantile groups using Stata's rule; ties stay together; grouped data masks default to integer codes
